text: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
The more they called them, the further they went away; they sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to idols.
Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk, who took them in my arms; but they did not know that I healed them.
I led them with cords of human kindness, with bonds of love. I was to them like one who lifts the yoke from their jaws, and I bent down to feed them.
He will not return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria shall be his king, because they refused to repent.
The sword will whirl through his cities, destroy the bars of his gates, and devour them because of their schemes.
My people are bent on turning away from me. Though they call to the Most High, not one of them will exalt him.

versions.text: My people are bent on turning from me. Though they call on the Most High, he will not lift them up.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew יַ֖חַד ("together / not one at all") is left untranslated, and the object/subject of יְרוֹמֵם is reversed. The verb is most naturally read as the people failing to exalt God, not God failing to lift them. The revision keeps the emphatic "not one" and preserves natural oral rhythm.

text: How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I treat you like Admah, or make you like Zeboiim? My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender.
I will not carry out my burning anger; I will not destroy Ephraim again. For I am God and not man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in wrath.

versions.text: I will not act on my burning anger; I will not turn to destroy Ephraim again. For I am God and not man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in wrath.
versions.explanation: אָשׁוּב followed by an infinitive functions adverbially ("again"), so "turn to destroy ... again" is redundant and stumbles when read aloud. "Carry out" also renders אֶעֱשֶׂה ("execute") more naturally than "act on."

versions.text: I will not carry out my burning anger; I will not destroy Ephraim again.
versions.explanation: The entire second half of the verse is missing from the current text. The Hebrew continues: כִּי אֵל אָנֹכִי וְלֹא־אִישׁ ("For I am God and not man"), בְּקִרְבְּךָ קָדוֹשׁ ("the Holy One in your midst"), וְלֹא אָבוֹא בְּעִיר ("and I will not come in wrath"). This clause carries the theological heart of the passage — the ground of God's restraint — and must be restored. The wording is taken from the earlier revision, preserving the intentional changes to the first half ("carry out" and the adverbial "again").

text: They shall follow the LORD; he will roar like a lion. When he roars, his children will come trembling from the west.
They will come trembling like a bird from Egypt, like a dove from the land of Assyria, and I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.

versions.text: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt, like doves from the land of Assyria, and I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.
versions.explanation: Both similes are singular in Hebrew (צִפּוֹר, יוֹנָה). The singular images are more vivid and match the source; the plural is an unnecessary adjustment.
